title: Microsoft Copilot Studio: workflow agent node can return generated files
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned file output from the workflow behaviour and credit controls Microsoft documents today. No actionable factual errors were found; small corrections would complete a navigation heading, cite the connector controls and align the checklist with its controls table.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans generated PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and CSV files as Agent node workflow outputs.
claims.quote: The Agent node can now return files that the agent generates, such as PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and CSV, as workflow outputs.

claims.claim: The planned files output works with inline agents.
claims.quote: Works with both inline agents and existing (published) agents.

claims.claim: The planned files output works with existing published agents.
claims.quote: Works with both inline agents and existing (published) agents.

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio workflow Agent node generate files Copilot Credits billing rate. Opened billing-credit-overview, manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness and workflows-credit-consumption; action and general AI billing are documented, but no file-output-specific rate.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant prevents consumption of unallocated prepaid tenant capacity beyond the environment allocation.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Cost and licensing: Caps; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Exhausting an environment's allocation does not stop usage if tenant-capacity draw or linked pay-as-you-go billing remains available.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing. ... If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: A published environment-group tenant-pool rule makes the environment-level setting read-only.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: API updates overriding a published group rule fail with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: Changing and republishing the environment-group rule is a documented way to change its governed setting.
claims.quote: Change and republish the rule for the environment group, or remove the environment from the group to manage the setting independently.

claims.claim: Removing an environment from the group restores independent editing of the setting.
claims.quote: After removal, the environment retains the value last applied by the group, but the setting becomes editable.

claims.claim: An agent-level monthly limit with Stop usage turns the agent off when it reaches the limit.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing: Caps; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Agent limits are not applied instantly and agents can continue responding for some time after reaching them.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: The agent-limit configuration also includes a notification threshold.
claims.quote: Select the agent, and then select Set limit. ... Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit. ... Configure the notification threshold.

claims.claim: The environment allocation control is at Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: Select the Summary tab. ... Under the Copilot Studio heading, select Manage Copilot Credits or Manage sessions. ... In the allocation panel, select an environment ... Under Capacity overages ... Select Draw from the available capacity in my tenant
claims.fix: Add the omitted heading: set controls[0].ui.path and its rendered path to 'Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes allocations and sets tenant-capacity draw through allocatedEntitlements[].enforcementRules with ruleType TenantPool and enabled false.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01"; @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false } ... Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The monthly agent limit is reached through Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents > agent > Set limit.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... On the Summary tab, select Manage Agents. ... You can set a monthly limit for any agent directly from this page.

claims.claim: No automation operation for setting the individual agent monthly credit limit is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent monthly consumption limit Stop usage API Dataverse bot table Power Platform licensing API limit; REST Power Platform agent monthly credit limit update. Opened pac copilot-studio and searched bot entity reference; no deciding limit property or operation found.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no UI or API switch specifically disabling files output from the workflow Agent node.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Agent node files output disable Power Platform API pac admin Dataverse bot entity reference; workflow Agent node files output default enable disable switch. Opened agent-node-workflow, pac copilot-studio; searched bot reference. No file-output switch found.

claims.claim: Credit controls apply across Copilot Studio, and shared-capacity changes can affect other agents, workflows and features in the environment.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. ... Changes to shared capacity can affect other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in the same environment.

claims.claim: Credit allocations and agent limits govern consumption, not the files an agent produces or their destination.
claims.quote: Credit allocations and agent limits control consumption. They don't control who is an approved author or who can open the Copilot Studio portal.

claims.claim: The conversation created-files preview documents a 10 MB size limit per created file.
claims.quote: | Size per created file | 10 MB |

claims.claim: The conversation created-files preview documents a 28-day retention period.
claims.quote: | Retention (per conversation) | 28 days after the last activity in the conversation |

claims.claim: Connector controls exist for Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.
claims.fix: Add 'Configure data policies for agents', https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention, to sources to support the rationale's statement that connector controls exist.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to change a published environment-group rule, but the controls table has no row for that group-level control.
claims.quote: Where a published environment-group rule governs that setting, change the group rule instead. ... Controls rows: environment credit allocation and tenant draw; individual agent monthly limit; file-output switch.
claims.fix: Remove 'Where a published environment-group rule governs that setting, change the group rule instead.' from the first Before rollout bullet. Retain the already documented group-rule qualification in Cost and licensing and controls[0].note; do not add a controls row.

claims.claim: Azure budgets and alerts notify administrators but do not stop Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness experiences are charged Copilot Credits for the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.
